description:
Israeli attacks on the southern Lebanese city of Tyre have killed at least eight people after the military issued a blanket evacuation order covering the entire coastal city, including its historic Christian quarter. Rescue teams continued searching for survivors in a residential area struck earlier, with fears the death toll could rise. The latest order instructs residents of Tyre, surrounding towns and Palestinian refugee camps to move north of the Zahrani River. It marks the first time residents of the predominantly Christian quarter have been ordered to leave, triggering panic and a new wave of displacement. Local officials say shelters are already full, leaving many with nowhere to go. Tyre has largely become a ghost town as businesses remain shut and residents fear further strikes. More than 1.2 million people have been displaced across Lebanon since the escalation of hostilities in October last year.

Al Jazeera’s Obaida Hitto reports from Tyre, southern Lebanon.

description:
In an interview with Al Jazeera, Gideon Levy, a columnist for the Israeli newspaper Haaretz, discussed Israel's domestic political landscape following direct missile strikes between Israel and Iran. 
He noted that Israel is not in a position to say no to US President Donald Trump, and that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is especially unable to defy him. 
Levy stated that Israel's dependence on the United States has reached an unprecedented level, as Israel cannot attack Iran without US support and has become an isolated "pariah state" that cannot lose its last ally.
Regarding Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz's vow to hit Hezbollah at full strength, Levy said such rhetoric is aimed at the central committee of his party for electoral primaries, not at actual policy. 
On public consensus, Levy observed that while support for war with Iran had reached 93 percent, he believes that support is now decreasing due to war fatigue and a slow realization that nothing was achieved in Gaza,

Trump told reporters that the accord would prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons and lead to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz immediately after signing. Trump argued that a negotiated settlement would be stronger than further military action, warning that additional bombing would cause significant loss of life and delay the reopening of key shipping routes. He also described the blockade imposed during the crisis as more effective than air strikes in pressuring Iran. Trump maintained there were no major obstacles remaining in the talks and expressed confidence that a “strong and powerful” agreement was close.

A desperate search and rescue operation is underway in the southern Philippines after a massive 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck the island of Mindanao. The powerful tremor, which hit just 13 kilometers southwest of General Santos City, has killed at least 37 people and injured over 200 others.  

As the 24-hour mark passes, the military has been deployed to aid emergency workers racing against time to pull survivors from collapsed buildings, including a severely damaged supermarket and shopping mall. While miraculous escapes were reported—such as employees and patrons managing to flee a local fast-food restaurant just moments before it flattened—authorities fear the casualty toll could still rise as teams clear structural debris.
